title: The Biggest Pro-AI Super PAC Network Has Poured Millions Into Nevada Shell Companies
key_facts: Lantern Production Consultants LLC has been paid around $20 million since last year by Think Big, part of a network of pro-AI super PACs funded by the Leading the Future PAC; its listed address is a post office box in a shopping centre in Sparks, Nevada (WIRED, from federal campaign finance records).

It is one of four Nevada LLCs paid by the network; Summit Ridge Media Group received about $13 million from American Mission between Dec 2025 and Sep 2026 and lists a Reno mail center; Blue Horizon Compliance Consultants lists a Staples store in Reno; Prusik Partners lists a Henderson strip mall.
The network, also based in Nevada, has raised over $140 million to influence the midterm elections.
Nevada's secretary of state told WIRED it could not locate any records for the businesses.

In May the Campaign Legal Center filed a complaint with the Federal Election Commission (FEC) alleging Think Big and American Mission broke federal law by failing to disclose the actual recipients of payments; its senior legal counsel Shanna Ports said 'This is about hiding where the money is going'.
The FEC has lacked the four commissioners it needs for a quorum since May 2025, so the complaint is unlikely to be heard soon, and the payments continue.

Leading the Future spokesperson Jesse Hunt said 'We comply with all applicable laws' and called the complaint a ploy by Public First, Anthropic and aligned groups; Public First and the Campaign Legal Center deny involvement and Anthropic did not respond.
The network funds both parties, Think Big mostly Democrats and American Mission Republicans; WIRED notes reasons to hide vendors range from benign to nefarious.
quote_evidence: Lantern Production Consultants has been paid around $20 million since last year by Think Big, part of a network of pro-AI super PACs funded by the Leading the Future PAC, for a wide array of services, including polling, digital advertising, research, and strategy, according to federal campaign finance records reviewed by WIRED.
Nevada’s secretary of state told WIRED that they were unable to locate any records for the businesses.
why_it_matters_hint: Voters cannot see who the biggest pro-AI political money is really paid to, and the election regulator cannot act without a quorum.
event_date: Published 13 Oct 2026 (updated 2:15 pm ET); payments Dec 2025 to Sep 2026; complaint filed May 2026.
